title: Tav (Shabbat 104a)
hook: emet, truth, uses the first, middle and last letters: truth spans everything

segments.voice: Yesterday, shin, the letter on the doorpost. Your line: shin on the door. Today, the last letter of the alef-bet.

Write the Hebrew word for a lie: sheker. Three letters, shin, kuf, resh. In the alef-bet they sit right next to each other near the end, crowded together. Now write the word for truth: emet. Alef, mem, tav. Alef stands at the very start, tav at the very end, mem between them. To spell the truth, you have to reach across the whole thing. The rabbis noticed this, and they didn't think it was an accident. Today, the letter that finishes the word, and the alef-bet.
screen: `SHEKER: THREE NEIGHBORS.` → `EMET: ALEF, MEM, TAV.` → `ACROSS THE WHOLE ALEF-BET.`

segments.voice: Tav makes a t sound, it's the last of the letters, and in tractate Shabbat the rabbis read the end of the alef-bet like a parable. Four readings. First, the span. Emet starts with the first letter, passes through the middle, and ends with the last. Truth, the reading goes, has to be true at the beginning, the middle and the end. A story honest only at the start isn't emet. Second, the crowd. The letters of sheker huddle together in one corner. The Talmud asks why, and answers: falsehood is easy to come by, and truth is hard to find. Lies are close at hand; truth takes a reach. Third, the feet. The letters of sheker, the rabbis say, each stand on a single leg. The letters of emet stand on broad bases, like bricks. Put simply: truth stands, and falsehood does not stand. A lie needs propping up; truth can bear weight. Fourth, the seal. Elsewhere in the same tractate, the Talmud says the seal of the Holy One is emet, truth. A seal is the mark at the end of a letter that says who it's from, and tav, the last letter, is where the seal goes. So the run of letters that began with a silent alef closes here, and the rabbis put truth across the whole span between them.
screen: `EMET: FIRST, MIDDLE, LAST.` · `SHEKER: NEIGHBORS IN A CORNER.` · `TRUTH STANDS; FALSEHOOD DOES NOT.` · `THE SEAL OF THE HOLY ONE IS TRUTH.` · then, large: `TRUTH FROM ALEF TO TAV.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one small place where you've been leaning on a lie: not a scandal, an I'm fine that isn't, a yes you didn't mean, a story you've been telling yourself. Notice how much effort it takes to keep it standing on one leg, then find the true sentence that could stand on its own feet and say it silently to yourself. If you pray, you can ask for courage.
Tav. The last letter of the alef-bet, the end of emet, truth, and in the Talmud's words, the seal of the Holy One. Today's word.
Your line: truth from alef to tav. Truth reaches the whole way. That's the whole alef-bet.

howItsDone: Jewish learners study the letters of emet and sheker through the Talmud's teaching in Shabbat 104a; the word emet is also said in daily prayer right after the Shema.

notes: Shabbat 104a and 55a paraphrased throughout; no quotation marks. Confirm the paraphrases (sheker's letters close together, falsehood common and truth rare; one leg vs. firm base; truth stands, falsehood does not).

The 'first, middle, last' reading of emet is from the index; in the classical sources it is most explicit in the Jerusalem Talmud (Sanhedrin 1:1) and Genesis Rabbah 81. Mem is the middle letter only if the five final forms are counted (27 letters); the script says only that mem 'stands between them'. Confirm.
'Twenty-two days of letters that began with a silent alef' was cut to avoid a count; the line now says the letters 'began with a silent alef'. Check the final wording.
howItsDone: 'emet' said right after the Shema (emet v'yatziv / emet ve'emunah). Confirm phrasing.
